analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown - October 23, 2026
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% on the week. Drivers cited: the start of mega-cap tech earnings, a mixed macro backdrop (oil up, rates down), and the debate over how durable the AI infrastructure trade is. AI-At-Risk, AI Software and Alternative Asset Managers outperformed. Goldminers, Copper and IPPs underperformed.

Prime book: US equities were net sold for a third straight week (4 of the last 5). Long and short sales in single stocks produced the largest de-grossing since late July. Industrials were among the most net sold sectors, with hedge funds selling the group at the fastest pace in more than 6 months. Staples and Real Estate were by far the most net bought, which points to a defensive posture.

Cash equities: long-only and hedge fund clients were moderate net sellers, with supply concentrated in tech. The GS floor has seen about $20bn of net TMT selling over 2 weeks across all client types and channels. That approaches the -$23bn over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode. Unlike the prior week, there was very little rotation into defensives despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and parts of Financials.

Brent options: Managed Money initiated significant long call positions in Brent through mid-October. Of the $2.3bn in new gross longs from Oct 6 to Oct 13, 32% were calls. Brent 3-month normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened and the ratio of 4 delta to 50 delta call implied volatility rose. Managed Money bought about $1bn more through Oct 20 as the US, Iran and Israel plan for a return to military engagement. Dealers and market makers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Thursday saw capitulation and de-grossing on AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record and is at its lowest since April of last year.

Vol retraced sharply early in the week into VIX expiry after last Friday's vol spike, then rebuilt with a steadier bid. Vol of vol is at its highest since April (83rd percentile, 3-year lookback). The NDX-SPX implied vol spread widened to near 5-year highs (98th percentile) because the losses were concentrated in tech.
The GS AI vs AI-At-Risk pair (GSPUARTI) is down 13% on the year. The S&P ex AI index (SPXXAI) has passed the S&P 500 on YTD returns.

The desk sees a hedge fund deleveraging episode in which short-term stops matter more than medium-term value. Its work on momentum and AI valuations says to buy the dip and selectively add back to the AI complex, starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber.

TMT: NDX finished the week down 80bps. The GS TMT Broad AI Basket fell 4.1% and the TMT Mo' Basket fell 7.8%. Client debate focused on the single driver of price action (oil, earnings sell-the-news in META, LRCX, TTMI and WDC, or positioning) and on what would turn the story around (the election, easing macro headwinds, AI data points). There is growing appetite for non-AI, idiosyncratic TMT ideas, seen in recent Consumer stock moves.
TMT earnings next week: Hyperscalers, Semis bellwethers (INTC, SNDK, STX, SEC/Hynix), and ORCL's analyst day.

Financials: A barbell of high-quality defensives (P&C insurance, card networks, senior housing REITs) and cheap/value risk-on names (regional banks, mid-cap payments with GAAP earnings, lodging REITs, life insurance) outperformed. Life insurance began to weaken late in the week as credit spreads and investment portfolios returned to focus. Blackstone's caution on real estate was followed by an 8% rally in the stock. The large rate decline drove a broad REIT rally.

Financials next week: card networks (MA, V, with V's guide in focus), senior housing REITs, more alternative managers, and insurance brokers, whose charts show a potential breakout if earnings go well.

Industrials fell 150bps against a broader market down 30bps. Materials led, up 125bps, as geopolitical tension kept inflation fears and commodity prices elevated. Notable moves: BMI +20% (short covering), EQPT +19% (pre-announced beat and raise), ALLE and POOL +15% (better-than-feared earnings), AVEX -28% (a large US Navy product under scrutiny), CRS -25% (rare miss and guide down), FPS -22% (AI/data center weakness and a CFO departure).
Industrials earnings next week: more than 50% of the space reports, alongside the FOMC.

Healthcare: price action reflected pre-set thematic playbooks more than EPS updates. Tools/CROs benefit from AI due-diligence themes. Medtech sees interest in a catch-up trade. Managed Care is still positioning around the Midterms. Earnings puts and takes: ABT lower organic guide, ISRG light US procedures, DHR guide cut on respiratory.

MRNA fell 17.5% and MRK fell 1.8% on Thursday after the leak and confirmation of its INT data. The headline recurrence-free survival hazard ratio of 0.58 cleared the previewed bar of below 0.6, but the stock reversed on sell-the-news dynamics. The desk saw bears re-engage on points including a lower actual HR bar, RCC data into year-end, implied oncology platform value, and commercialization execution risk.

US fundamental long/short net leverage (beta adjusted) is down 21 points from the June highs and near 3-year lows (5th percentile). Gross leverage looks balanced (42nd percentile 1-year, 56th percentile 3-year).

EWZ 1-month normalized put-call skew keeps rising and is at all-time highs ahead of the Brazil election this weekend. The desk saw interest in EWZ upside via calls and call spreads, and in GSBZRATE for a higher-beta play.
